messages:
rachel (People Ops): Quick one  Tom converted from full-time to contractor mid-year and also relocated (US->UK) during the payroll provider cutover window. He stopped 401(k) and HSA deductions on the FTE->contractor conversion date. Can we: 1) remit employer match for the period he was an employee before conversion, 2) treat catch-up (age 50+) for any amounts withheld, and 3) are there vendor/legal or contractor-specific blockers for making a retro payment after cutover?
sam (Payroll): Need dates to assess vendor windows. What were: FTE->contractor conversion effective date, last US pay date, payroll cutover date? Also note: contractors are not eligible for the US 401(k) going forward, but that doesn't prevent remitting employer match for periods when he was eligible as an employee. Legacy vendor accepts retro deposits for actual deferrals if within their reconciliation/cutoff window.
rachel (People Ops): Conversion effective 2025-07-30 (contractor effective next sprint), last US employee paycheck 2025-07-24 (paid), payroll cutover with new vendor 2025-08-12. Tom turned 50 on 2025-05-10. He stopped HSA same day he converted.
sam (Payroll): With that timeline we might still be inside the vendor's post-cutover reconciliation window but will need to confirm. What we will need: signed authorization from employee, payroll export showing elective deferrals and any catch-up withheld for Jan->07/24, ssn_last4, legacy payroll id, and a remittance instruction from finance. If vendor requires a quarter cutoff exception we'll escalate.
priya (Finance): From accounting perspective: employer match is an expense attributable to the wage period when deferrals occurred, but we book when remitted. We can fund a manual remittance (GL 6810) once payroll confirms vendor acceptance. Important: because the employee converted to contractor, check how we classify the payment on reporting; we may need to tag memo "retro match for employee pay periods". Also loop legal for any cross-border / contractor tax treatment concerns.
tom (Employee): Thanks. I had elected catch-up earlier and some was withheld. Am I eligible to have catch-up remitted for the full annual limit even though I converted?
sam (Payroll): You can only have catch-up remitted for amounts actually withheld while you were on employee payroll. The plan's catch-up limit is annual per IRS, but we cannot create withheld amounts that weren't elected. If you had catch-up withheld through 07/24 we'll remit those withheld amounts to the legacy plan. No new catch-up contributions can be added post-conversion without payroll withholding.
401k-bot: Policy excerpt: "Employer match is calculated on elective deferrals actually remitted to the plan during the plan year. Catch-up contributions follow IRS rules and require amounts to be withheld on payroll. Contractors are ineligible for ongoing plan participation; retro remits for prior employee periods may be accepted per vendor cutover terms. Contact payroll@redwood with required docs." <https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/401k-cutover-guidance>
rachel (People Ops): Action items: I'll collect the payroll export for 2025-01-01 -> 2025-07-24 and secure Tom's signed authorization template. Priya  can you pre-authorize funding estimate so payroll can submit remittance? Sam  please open a vendor recon ticket when I post the docs. We'll loop legal if vendor flags cross-border or contractor reporting issues.
priya (Finance): Will pre-authorize a provisional remittance after we get the payroll export estimate. Please include the company match formula used (e.g., 50% up to 6% or flat 3% etc.) and cost center.
sam (Payroll): Will open vendor ticket (ref TKT-401K-CTR-2114) when docs posted. If vendor requires block because conversion to contractor affects plan eligibility, I'll escalate to vendor ops + legal.
rachel (People Ops): Thanks everyone 44d I'll DM Tom the manual remit template and upload the CSV when ready. Tom  please sign and return by EOD so we can meet vendor window.
